thread.title: U.S. Stock Market Dives On Troubling News | Investor's Business Daily

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: U.S. Stock Market Dives On Troubling News | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks tried to find the day's bottom late Thursday morning, as the stock market sold off hard.
X The chief catalyst wasn't clear, given the long lineup of suspects: a China hack of computer hardware, a big jump in a job cuts report and a U.S. Treasury 10-year bond sell-off that drove the 10-year yield to as high as 3.2%.
The Nasdaq dived 1.7%, while the Dow Jones industrial average and the S&P 500 carved off 0.9% to 1.1% each. Small caps as gauged by the Russell 2000 fell nearly 1%.
Volume dipped on the NYSE but expanded sharply on the Nasdaq compared to the same time Wednesday.
Among IBD's 197 industry groups, a battle of the laggards was underway. The biggest losers included lowly rated groups such as chip equipment makers, homebuilders and gaming software. Other mediocre-ranked groups comprised the day's winners: banks, medical supplies and gold miners.

JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) surged 1.3%, heading toward its fourth daily gain in a row. But the stock reversed to a 0.6% gain. Western Alliance Bancorp ( WAL ) popped 2% as it tried to retake its 200-day moving average. The stock then reversed to a 0.9% gain. SVB Financial ( SIVB ) added 1.4% as it closed in on a 333.84 correct buy point but then reversed to a 0.1% gain. SVB is trading about 3% off its high.
The recent rise in interest rates is regarded as bullish for bank stocks. Higher interest rates help banks in two ways. Net interest margins grow, boosting the bottom line. Also, banks are more apt to approve more loans when margins are greater.
Despite the bullish logic, the bank sector hasn't done all that well this year. Going into Thursday's session, the bank sector was No. 28 among 33 sectors in the IBD stock research tables . The closely related savings and loan sector is dead last.
Report Of China Hack A Bloomberg News report of a China hack of computer hardware also weighed on the market. Super Micro Computer ( SMCI ), which trades on the over-the-counter Nasdaq market, dropped more than 56% to 9.35 in heavy volume. Bloomberg News said China sabotaged Super Micro components manufactured in China, adding a tiny chip that ultimately affected 30 companies.
Super Micro, Amazon Web Services and Apple ( AAPL ), which all use Super Micro components, denied the Bloomberg report.
Amazon.com ( AMZN ) dropped 1.5%, while Apple sagged 1%.
Financial Data Challenger, Gray & Christmas reported a 44% jump in planned job cuts. Half of the cuts were tied to Well Fargo 's ( WFC ) plan to ax 5% to 10% of its workforce.
Factory orders in August rose 2.3%, topping the consensus view for 2.1%.
First-time jobless claims rolled in at 207,000, about 3% fewer than expected.
